title: Build a REST HTTP server in Go — 4 turns
description: Four-turn REST server: turn 1 GET /items list, turn 2 POST /items create, turn 3 DELETE /items/:id, turn 4 full test suite.

task_spec.prompt: Implement `GET /items` in the `ServeHTTP` method of `Handler` in `server/server.go`. Check `r.Method == http.MethodGet` and `r.URL.Path == "/items"`. Call `h.store.List()` and encode the result as JSON with status 200. Run `go test ./...` — focus on getting TestListEmpty to pass.
followup_prompts: Good progress. Run `go test ./...` to see where we stand. Now add `POST /items`: decode `{"name": "..."}` from the request body, call `h.store.Create(name)`, and respond with 201 + the created item as JSON. Continue with the remaining steps.
Good. Now add `DELETE /items/:id`: parse the ID from the path (e.g., `/items/3`), call `h.store.Delete(id)`, respond 204 on success or 404 if not found. Run `go test ./...` to check.
Final push: run `go test ./...` and fix any remaining failures. Make sure all 5 tests pass — list, create, list-after-create, delete, and delete-not-found.
success_criteria: GET /items returns JSON array (empty or populated)
POST /items creates item with auto-incremented ID, returns 201
